source_text:
Ὁρᾶτε, ἀγαπητοι, πῶς μεγα καὶ θαυμαστόν ἐστιν ἡ ἀγάπη, καὶ τῆς τελειότητος αὐτῆς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐξήγησις.
τίς ἱκανὸς ἐν αὐτῇ εὑρεθῆναι, εἰ μὴ οὓς ἂν καταξιώσῃ ὁ θεός; δεώμεθα οὖν καὶ αἰτώμεθα ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐλέους αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἐν ἀγάπῃ εὑρεθῶμεν δίχα προσκλίσεως ἀνθρωπίνης, ἄμωμοι.
αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ ἕως τῆσδε τῆς ἡμέρας παρῆλθον, ἀλλ’ οἱ ἐν ἀγάπῃ τελειωθέντες κατὰ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ χάριν ἔχουσιν χῶρον εὐσεβῶν, οἳ φανερωθήσονται ἐν τῇ ἐπισκοπῇ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
γέγραπται γάρ: Εἰσέλθετε εἰς τὰ ταμεῖα μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ἕως οὖ παρέλθῃ ἡ ὀργὴ καὶ ὁ θυμός μου, καὶ μνησθήσομαι ἡμέρας ἀγαθῆς, καὶ ἀναστήσω ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῶν θηκῶν ὑμῶν.
μακάριοί ἐσμεν, ἀγαπητοί, εἰ τὰ προστάγματα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐποιοῦμεν ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ ἀγάπης, εἰς τὸ ἀφεθῆναι ἡμῖν δἰ ἀγάπης τὰς ἁμαρτίας.
γέγραπται γάρ: Μακάριοι, ὦν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι: μακάριος ἀνήρ, οὖ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν, οὐδέ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ δόλος:
οὗτος ὁ μακαρισμὸς ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐκλελεγμένους ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: Love's perfection and the blessedness of the forgiven
orientation: Clement has just praised love at length and now turns to the greatness of love, the need to be found in it without human partiality, and the blessedness of those whose sins are forgiven through love.
pass_a_gloss: See, beloved, how great and wonderful is love, and of its perfection there is no explanation. Who is sufficient to be found in it, except those whom God should deem worthy? Let us ask therefore and request from his mercy, that in love we may be found without human inclination, blameless. All generations from Adam until this day passed away, but those perfected in love according to the grace of God have a place of the pious, who will be made manifest in the visitation of the kingdom of Christ. For it is written: Enter into the chambers a little while, until my anger and wrath should pass by, and I will remember a good day, and I will raise you from your tombs. Blessed are we, beloved, if we were doing the commandments of God in harmony of love, for the forgiveness to us through love of sins. For it is written: Blessed are those whose lawless deeds were forgiven and whose sins were covered; blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not reckon, nor is there deceit in his mouth. This blessing came upon those chosen by God through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom be glory to the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: The noun means leaning or inclination toward someone; 'partiality' captures the sense of favoritism that would compromise blamelessness.
χῶρος is a region or place; 'among the pious' renders the genitive as belonging to or shared with the pious.
ἐπισκοπή here means a divine visitation or oversight, not the office of bishop; 'visitation' preserves the eschatological sense.
The word means inner rooms or store-chambers; 'chambers' is the standard rendering for this Isaiah quotation.
ὁμόνοια is the glossary term 'harmony'; the genitive ἀγάπης specifies the kind of harmony.
The perfect participle of ἐκλέγομαι means those who have been chosen; 'chosen' is plain and matches the glossary's 'the elect' family.

bible_refs.note: Εἰσέλθετε εἰς τὰ ταμεῖα μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ἕως οὖ παρέλθῃ ἡ ὀργὴ καὶ ὁ θυμός μου
Μακάριοι, ὦν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι: μακάριος ἀνήρ, οὖ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν, οὐδέ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ δόλος

pass_b_english: You see, beloved, how great and wonderful love is. Its perfection is beyond all explanation. Who is able to be found in it, except those whom God deems worthy? Let us ask and plead from his mercy, then, that we may be found in love without human partiality, blameless.

All the generations from Adam until this day have passed away. But those who were perfected in love according to the grace of God hold a place among the pious. They will be made manifest at the visitation of the kingdom of Christ. For it is written: "Enter the chambers for a little while, until my anger and wrath pass by" (Isaiah 26:20), "and I will remember a good day and raise you up from your tombs."

We are blessed, beloved, if we do the commandments of God in the harmony of love, so that our sins may be forgiven us through love. For it is written: "Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not count, and in whose mouth there is no deceit" (Psalm 32:1-2).
This blessing came upon the elect of God through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

polish.changed: Broke long sentences into clearer units, made the implied subject of the blessing explicit, and smoothed the flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and quotation.

Clarified that 'the elect' refers to the same group throughout, removed the inconsistent 'Master/Lord' alternation by keeping 'Lord' for God, and smoothed sentence flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.why: Key concept rendered inconsistently; reader may miss that all refer to the same group.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'the elect' or 'the elect of God' throughout.

notes.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
notes.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'the elect of God' is real: the English uses 'those who were chosen by God' instead of the standardized term 'the elect of God'. Fixed.
The glossary issue about 'the Master' is not present in this passage: the English consistently uses 'Lord' for God and Christ, with no occurrence of 'Master'.

problems.quote: This blessing came upon the elect through Jesus Christ our Lord
problems.source_quote: οὗτος ὁ μακαρισμὸς ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐκλελεγμένους ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν
problems.why: The blessing rests on those God chose through Christ; English drops God's choosing and attaches 'through Christ' to the blessing.
problems.fix: This blessing came upon those chosen by God through Jesus Christ our Lord
problems.ruling: Source 'ἐκλελεγμένους ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ' means elect chosen by God; English 'the elect' drops 'ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ', and 'through Jesus Christ' is ambiguous.

edits.old: This blessing came upon the elect through Jesus Christ our Lord
edits.new: This blessing came upon the elect of God through Jesus Christ our Lord

fixed: Added 'of God' for ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, keeping glossary 'the elect' for τοὺς ἰκλελεγμένους and 'διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν' with the elect; did not use suggested 'those chosen by God'.

problems.quote: "Enter the chambers for a little while, until my anger and wrath pass by, and I will remember a good day and raise you up from your tombs" (Isaiah 26:20).
problems.source_quote: Εἰσέλθετε εἰς τὰ ταμεῖα μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, ἕως οὖ παρέλθῃ ἡ ὀργὴ καὶ ὁ θυμός μου, καὶ μνησθήσομαι ἡμέρας ἀγαθῆς, καὶ ἀναστήσω ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῶν θηκῶν ὑμῶν.
problems.why: Only the chambers image echoes Isaiah 26:20. The good day and raising from tombs are not in that verse.
problems.fix: "Enter the chambers for a little while, until my anger and wrath pass by" (Isaiah 26:20), "and I will remember a good day and raise you up from your tombs."
problems.ruling: Only 'εἰς τὰ ταμεῖα… ἕως οὖ παρέλθῃ ἡ ὀργή' echoes Isa 26:20. 'ἀναστήσω ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῶν θηκῶν' echoes Ezek 37:12. Labelling the whole composite as Isaiah 26:20 misleads.

edits.old: For it is written: "Enter the chambers for a little while, until my anger and wrath pass by, and I will remember a good day and raise you up from your tombs" (Isaiah 26:20).
edits.new: For it is written: "Enter the chambers for a little while, until my anger and wrath pass by" (Isaiah 26:20), "and I will remember a good day and raise you up from your tombs."

fixed: wrong_scripture: fixed — only εἰσέλθετε εἰς τὰ ταμεῖα ... ἕως οὖ παρέλθῃ ἡ ὀργῆ καὶ ὁ θυμός μου echoes Isaiah 26:20; καὶ μνησθήσομαι ἡμέρας ἀγαθῆς, καὶ ἀναστήσω ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῶν θηκῶν ὑμῶν is not in that verse, so restricted citation to first clause.

last_rejected.quote: This blessing came upon the elect of God through Jesus Christ our Lord
last_rejected.source_quote: οὗτος ὁ μακαρισμὸς ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐκλελεγμένους ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν
last_rejected.why: διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ marks how God chose them, not how the blessing arrived.
last_rejected.fix: This blessing came upon those chosen by God through Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐκλελεγμένους ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: the διὰ phrase is ambiguous; 'came upon the elect … through Jesus Christ' is a defensible rendering, mirroring 1 Clement 50.7.
